title: IVs, DVs, models, and other stats lingo

cues.en: Instructor: I thought this would be a good time to introduce you to some lingo, some terminology that is often used in statistics.
cues.zh: 講師：現在很適合介紹一些統計中常用的行話、術語。

cues.en: And this goes just beyond defining a couple of terms.
cues.zh: 不只是定義幾個詞。

cues.en: I'm also going to be sharing with you a little bit of philosophy about how to think about doing statistics.
cues.zh: 也會分享一點關於如何思考統計的哲學。

cues.en: Okay, so let's start with some basic terms like IVs and DVs.
cues.zh: 先從 IV 和 DV 這些基本術語開始。

cues.en: I don't think they're actually pronounced like that.
cues.zh: 我想它們其實不是那樣唸。

cues.en: They're IVs and DVs.
cues.zh: 是逐字母唸的 IVs 和 DVs。

cues.en: So DV stands for dependent variable.
cues.zh: DV 代表 dependent variable，也就是依變數。

cues.en: It's also sometimes called the outcome variable.
cues.zh: 有時也稱為結果變數。

cues.en: And this is basically the variable in the data that you are trying to explain.
cues.zh: 基本上，就是資料中你試圖解釋的變數。

cues.en: And then we have the IVs or the independent variables, also sometimes called explanatory variables.
cues.zh: IV 則是 independent variable，也就是自變數，有時稱解釋變數。

cues.en: And these are the variables in the data that you hope will explain variance in the dependent variable.
cues.zh: 希望用這些資料變數，解釋依變數的變異。

cues.en: So the independent variables explain the dependent variables.
cues.zh: 所以自變數解釋依變數。

cues.en: If you are setting up an experiment and you have experimental manipulations, then it's the independent variables that you are manipulating.
cues.zh: 設定實驗、進行實驗操弄時，操弄的就是自變數。

cues.en: These are the things that you as the experimenter have control over, and this is what you are measuring.
cues.zh: 這些是實驗者能控制的，而這裡則是所測量的。

cues.en: Now, you don't always have control over the independent variables.
cues.zh: 不過，不是每次都能控制自變數。

cues.en: Sometimes the independent variables are things that you observe in the real world, and you hope that those are predicting things about the dependent variable.
cues.zh: 有時它們是現實世界中觀察到的事物，希望能藉此預測依變數。

cues.en: Okay, so I'm gonna walk through a few examples and what I would like you to do with each example is identify the two variables.
cues.zh: 接著看幾個例子，希望你在每個例子中找出兩個變數。

cues.en: So each example is gonna have two variables, one IV and one DV.
cues.zh: 每個例子都有兩個變數，一個 IV、一個 DV。

cues.en: And you should identify which variable is the IV and which is the DV.
cues.zh: 辨識哪個是自變數，哪個是依變數。

cues.en: So here we have our first example, the effects of soil moisture on plant growth.
cues.zh: 第一個例子，土壤濕度對植物生長的影響。

cues.en: Now, if you want a little bit of more time to think about this, then feel free to pause the video.
cues.zh: 如果需要多一點思考時間，可以暫停影片。

cues.en: Okay, so the two variables that we have here are soil moisture and plant growth.
cues.zh: 兩個變數是土壤濕度和植物生長。

cues.en: And soil moisture is the independent variable.
cues.zh: 土壤濕度是自變數。

cues.en: If we're doing this as an experiment, this is what we can control.
cues.zh: 如果做成實驗，這是可以控制的。

cues.en: We can change the soil moisture.
cues.zh: 可以改變土壤濕度。

cues.en: That's the independent variable.
cues.zh: 這是自變數。

cues.en: And we believe that the soil moisture affects the plant growth.
cues.zh: 我們相信，土壤濕度會影響植物生長。

cues.en: So the plant growth is the dependent variable.
cues.zh: 所以植物生長是依變數。

cues.en: It's the thing that we are trying to explain.
cues.zh: 是試圖解釋的事物。

cues.en: Here is a second example.
cues.zh: 第二個例子。

cues.en: The effects of time spent on Facebook on irritability.
cues.zh: 使用 Facebook 的時間，對易怒程度的影響。

cues.en: So do people become more irritable when they spend more time on Facebook?
cues.zh: 花更多時間在 Facebook，會變得更容易生氣嗎？

cues.en: So again, the two variables are time spent on Facebook and irritability, and what is the IV and what is the DV here?
cues.zh: 兩個變數是 Facebook 使用時間和易怒程度，哪個是 IV、哪個是 DV？

cues.en: Well, it seems to make sense to me that independent variable is going to be the time spent on Facebook, and the dependent variable will be irritability.
cues.zh: 我認為，自變數是 Facebook 使用時間，依變數是易怒程度，這樣合理。

cues.en: But you can see in this example, and you'll see it more in the next example, it's not always so clear which one is the independent variable and which one is dependent.
cues.zh: 但這個例子可以看出，下一個例子更明顯，並不是總能清楚判斷哪個自變、哪個依變。

cues.en: Sometimes there can be a little bit of ambiguity, sometimes it could go either way.
cues.zh: 有時有一點模糊，有時兩種方向都可能。

cues.en: Usually when you think about independent, which is the independent variable and which is the dependent variable, you wanna think about what is the likely flow
cues.zh: 通常思考哪個是自變數、哪個是依變數時，要想想真實世界中，可能的

cues.en: of causality in the world.
cues.zh: 因果方向。

cues.en: Now, in statistics, we have to be really careful when discussing causality, because just because we find an effect doesn't mean that there is a causal relationship
cues.zh: 統計中討論因果必須非常小心，因為發現某種效果，不表示兩者之間

cues.en: between them.
cues.zh: 有因果關係。

cues.en: Nonetheless, we can speculate about causality.
cues.zh: 但仍可以對因果提出推測。

cues.en: By the way, I will talk about this issue of causality much more in the section on correlation.
cues.zh: 順帶一提，相關那一章會更深入談因果問題。

cues.en: So here we can speculate.
cues.zh: 這裡可以推測。

cues.en: It seems reasonable to me that if you spend a lot more time on Facebook, you're going to become more irritable, but you could also imagine it the other way.
cues.zh: 我認為花更多時間在 Facebook，會更容易生氣，似乎合理，但也可以想成反方向。

cues.en: So maybe people who are just naturally more irritable, they tend to spend a lot more time on Facebook.
cues.zh: 也許本來就比較易怒的人，往往花更多時間在 Facebook。

cues.en: So you could go either way.
cues.zh: 所以兩個方向都可以。

cues.en: In my opinion, it makes more sense to have time spent on Facebook as the IV and irritability as a DV.
cues.zh: 我個人覺得，Facebook 使用時間作為 IV，易怒程度作為 DV，更合理。

cues.en: Now, when you see a construction of a research statement or hypothesis like this, so effects of blank on blank, then it's usually pretty clear
cues.zh: 看到像這樣「某事對某事的影響」的研究陳述或假設時，通常很清楚，

cues.en: that the effects of that's referring to the IV and the on it refers to the DV.
cues.zh: 「某事的影響」前面的因素指 IV，受到影響的對象指 DV。

cues.en: So that's a pretty clear way.
cues.zh: 這是一種很清楚的表達。

cues.en: Now, it's not always worded like that.
cues.zh: 但不一定這樣寫。

cues.en: It could be something like this relation between money spent on clothes and bar hopping.
cues.zh: 也可能是，買衣服花費與跑酒吧之間的關係。

cues.en: Okay, so here the two variables are the amount of money that someone spends on new clothes and how much time they spend bar hopping.
cues.zh: 兩個變數是買新衣服花多少錢，以及花多少時間跑酒吧。

cues.en: Maybe, how many bars they visit per week, something like that.
cues.zh: 也許是每週去幾間酒吧之類的。

cues.en: So what is the IV and what is the DV?
cues.zh: 哪個是 IV，哪個是 DV？

cues.en: Well, this one is also quite ambiguous.
cues.zh: 這個也很模糊。

cues.en: I could see this going either way.
cues.zh: 我覺得兩個方向都有可能。

cues.en: Maybe, we think that people who spend more money on clothes, they wanna show off their clothes, so they go out more often, or maybe so.
cues.zh: 也許買衣服花更多錢的人，想展示衣服，所以更常出門；或者。

cues.en: So therefore the IV would be money spent and the DV would be bar hopping.
cues.zh: 因此 IV 是花費，DV 是跑酒吧。

cues.en: We could also imagine it the other way.
cues.zh: 也可以反過來想。

cues.en: People who like to spend more time in bars want to look more presentable, so they end up spending more money on clothes.
cues.zh: 喜歡花更多時間在酒吧的人，希望外表更體面，所以買衣服花更多錢。

cues.en: So then this would be the IV, and this would be the DV.
cues.zh: 這個就會是 IV，那個是 DV。

cues.en: So you can see that sometimes it can go either way.
cues.zh: 所以有時兩個方向都可以。

cues.en: It depends a little bit on your thoughts, the assumptions you're bringing in to the experiment or to the research.
cues.zh: 有一點取決於你的想法，以及帶入實驗或研究的假設。

cues.en: And it also depends on how you want to interpret the data.
cues.zh: 也取決於想如何解讀資料。

cues.en: Sometimes it's more clear what the direction or which variable is the IV and which is the DV.
cues.zh: 有時方向，或者哪個是 IV、哪個是 DV，會比較清楚。

cues.en: So in terms of data visualization, it is common, it's common practice to have the independent variable on the x-axis and the dependent variable on the y-axis.
cues.zh: 資料視覺化中，慣例是把自變數放 X 軸、依變數放 Y 軸。

cues.en: So here's some examples.
cues.zh: 這裡有些例子。

cues.en: Time spent on Facebook and irritability, of course, these are just made up data.
cues.zh: Facebook 使用時間和易怒程度，當然只是虛構資料。

cues.en: And here is, let's say we are manipulating soil moisture in three bins, three groups.
cues.zh: 這裡假設把土壤濕度操弄成三個區間、三組。

cues.en: So this is like very dry, sort of medium wet, and this is wet and then here's plant growth.
cues.zh: 這是很乾、中等濕度，以及濕，這裡是植物生長。

cues.en: Now, I say the term usually here, because this is not a hard and fast rule.
cues.zh: 我說「通常」，因為不是鐵則。

cues.en: So you might see, for example, some people plotting data like this.
cues.zh: 例如，可能看到有人這樣畫。

cues.en: So here we have plant growth growth on the x-axis and soil moisture on the y-axis.
cues.zh: X 軸是植物生長，Y 軸是土壤濕度。

cues.en: So here the bars are going horizontal instead of vertical, but unless you have a compelling reason, otherwise, it's good practice to stick to the independent variable
cues.zh: 長條變成水平而非垂直，但除非有充分理由，否則最好遵循自變數

cues.en: on the x-axis and the outcome variable or the DV on the Y-axis.
cues.zh: 放 X 軸，結果變數或 DV 放 Y 軸的慣例。

cues.en: The next topic that I want you to discuss is models and a modeling.
cues.zh: 接下來談模型和建模。

cues.en: So what do you think models are?
cues.zh: 你認為模型是什麼？

cues.en: What, what comes to mind when you hear the word model?
cues.zh: 聽到 model 這個詞，想到什麼？

cues.en: Well, maybe it's something like this, but this is actually not the kind of model that we are thinking about in statistics, or at least that's not the kind of models
cues.zh: 也許是這種模特兒，但這不是統計中考慮的模型，至少不是

cues.en: that you should be thinking about when trying to learn statistics.
cues.zh: 學統計時應該想的那種。

cues.en: Instead, models are simplified representations of reality.
cues.zh: 模型是現實的簡化表示。

cues.en: The thing is, the universe is this unbelievably mindbogglingly complex place.
cues.zh: 宇宙是個難以置信、複雜到不可思議的地方。

cues.en: We as human beings are only just barely beginning to scratch the surface of understanding the true nature of the universe, of physics,
cues.zh: 我們人類對宇宙、物理真實本質的理解，才剛開始觸及表面，

cues.en: of biology, and so on.
cues.zh: 生物學等等也是如此。

cues.en: So we can't possibly hope to understand the universe in all of its mind-boggling complexity.
cues.zh: 不可能奢望理解宇宙所有令人難以想像的複雜性。

cues.en: So what we do instead is develop these simplified representations of reality that allow us to focus on important features of the world
cues.zh: 所以改成建立現實的簡化表示，讓我們專注於世界的重要特徵，

cues.en: while ignoring or abstracting away other features that are either less important for the question at hand, or less relevant or just not understood.
cues.zh: 同時忽略或抽象化其他對目前問題較不重要、不相關，或尚未理解的特徵。

cues.en: And so we relegate them to understanding in the future.
cues.zh: 把它們留到未來理解。

cues.en: So this would be the real world, and this would be our model of the real world.
cues.zh: 這是真實世界，這是我們對真實世界的模型。

cues.en: Beautiful, brilliant advertisement from Lego.
cues.zh: Lego 很漂亮、很精彩的廣告。

cues.en: So what does that mean in practice?
cues.zh: 實務上這是什麼意思？

cues.en: Well, a model in statistics is an equation or sometimes a set of equations that explains some feature in a dataset.
cues.zh: 統計模型是一個方程式，有時是一組方程式，解釋資料集中的某些特徵。

cues.en: So for example, let's say we are trying to understand why people are the height that they are.
cues.zh: 例如，試圖理解為什麼人們有這樣的身高。

cues.en: So, adults have, there's a large variety in heights.
cues.zh: 成年人的身高差異很大。

cues.en: Some people are shorter, some people are taller, and we wanna know why.
cues.zh: 有些人矮，有些人高，想知道為什麼。

cues.en: Well, that's a really complicated question, right?
cues.zh: 這是很複雜的問題，對吧？

cues.en: There's like many, many factors that determine how tall someone is as an adult.
cues.zh: 有非常多因素決定成年後身高。

cues.en: So let's say we come up with a model, it's a simplified version of reality.
cues.zh: 假設提出一個模型，也就是現實的簡化版本。

cues.en: So we say that our model consists of three variables.
cues.zh: 模型包含三個變數。

cues.en: So we say that height is related to your sex because men tend to be taller than women, it's related to your parents' height because people with tall parents are likely to be tall,
cues.zh: 身高和性別有關，因為男性通常比女性高；和父母身高有關，因為父母高的人往往也高，

cues.en: and it's related to child nutrition because people who eat healthy as a child tend to be taller as adults.
cues.zh: 也和兒童時期營養有關，因為小時候吃得健康，成年後往往較高。

cues.en: Okay, so this is our model of the world of height.
cues.zh: 這就是身高世界的模型。

cues.en: Now we know that there's many more variables that explain someone's height, and we could come up with them, maybe you can think of breaking down nutrition
cues.zh: 知道還有很多變數能解釋身高，也能想出來，例如把營養

cues.en: into different varieties, or you can have how much exercise you got as a kid, some other genetics factors, all sorts of complicated things.
cues.zh: 分成不同種類，或者小時候運動量、其他遺傳因素，各種複雜因素。

cues.en: But we're not trying to explain 100% of everything about height.
cues.zh: 但不是試圖解釋身高的一切、百分之百的細節。

cues.en: We are trying to come up with a simplified model, a simplified equation that captures the most relevant features for our particular research.
cues.zh: 而是提出一個簡化模型、簡化方程式，捕捉對特定研究最相關的特徵。

cues.en: Now, of course, these three variables are not going to explain every single thing.
cues.zh: 當然，這三個變數不會解釋每一件事。

cues.en: You know, it's not gonna explain every picometer of height.
cues.zh: 不會解釋身高的每一皮米。

cues.en: So therefore we add this term to the model, which is called the residual or the air.
cues.zh: 所以模型加入這一項，稱為殘差或誤差。

cues.en: And the idea is that all of the features in height, all of the differences in height that are not explained by sex, parents height and child
cues.zh: 所有未被性別、父母身高，以及兒童

cues.en: and nutrition go into this residual.
cues.zh: 營養解釋的身高特徵、身高差異，都會放進這個殘差。

cues.en: So this residual, these errors are really important for models and model fitting in statistics.
cues.zh: 這些殘差、誤差，對統計模型與模型擬合非常重要。

cues.en: So I wanna spend a little bit more time talking about models and about residuals.
cues.zh: 所以要多花一點時間，談模型和殘差。

cues.en: So the way that I think about models is like you have this template and that template is your model, and then you impose your template onto the real world
cues.zh: 我理解模型的方式是，有一個樣板，這樣板就是模型，再把它套到真實世界，

cues.en: and you want to see, does the real world match my template?
cues.zh: 看看真實世界是否符合樣板。

cues.en: And if it does, it's a good model, and if it doesn't, it's a crappy model.
cues.zh: 符合就是好模型，不符合就是糟模型。

cues.en: So I've tried to abstract that a little bit.
cues.zh: 我試著把這稍微抽象化。

cues.en: So let's say the real world, this is some abstract data space.
cues.zh: 假設真實世界，是某種抽象資料空間。

cues.en: The real world looks something like this, and we have our model, which looks something like this.
cues.zh: 真實世界像這樣，而模型像這樣。

cues.en: So now we compare the model to the data, which re represents the real world, and we wanna know how similar are these things.
cues.zh: 比較模型和代表真實世界的資料，想知道兩者多相似。

cues.en: So we can actually just subtract one from the other, and that's going to give us our residual.
cues.zh: 可以直接將一個減去另一個，得到殘差。

cues.en: And then the important question is how close is the, or how large is this residual?
cues.zh: 重要問題是，殘差有多接近，或者說有多大？

cues.en: If this residual is small, that means that the model fit the data really well.
cues.zh: 殘差小，表示模型非常符合資料。

cues.en: And so it's a good model.
cues.zh: 所以是好模型。

cues.en: And if the residual is large, then the model doesn't fit the data very well.
cues.zh: 殘差大，則表示模型不太符合資料。

cues.en: We need a new template. The model isn't very good.
cues.zh: 需要新樣板，模型不好。

cues.en: So that might lead you to think that we should make our models of the world be increasingly sophisticated.
cues.zh: 這可能讓你認為，世界模型應該越來越精密。

cues.en: We add more and more variables, and they make them more and more complicated.
cues.zh: 加入越來越多變數，變得越來越複雜。

cues.en: And that will get more and more towards the complexity of the real world.
cues.zh: 就能越來越接近真實世界的複雜性。

cues.en: But in statistics, there's a bit of a balance, or I should say in science in general, not just in statistics, there's a balance, there's a competition.
cues.zh: 但統計中，或者應該說一般科學，不只是統計，有一種平衡、一種競爭。

cues.en: We want the residuals to be small, which means that the model is good, but we also want the models to be simple.
cues.zh: 希望殘差小，代表模型好，但也希望模型簡單。

cues.en: We want the models to have simplicity and beauty so they can be easily interpreted and easily fit onto other data and explain other phenomenon.
cues.zh: 希望模型簡單、優美，容易解讀，也容易套用到其他資料、解釋其他現象。

cues.en: So there's always this competition that the residuals should be small, but the model should be simple.
cues.zh: 所以一直有這種競爭：殘差要小，但模型要簡單。

cues.en: When the model is too simple, the residuals get too large.
cues.zh: 模型太簡單，殘差就太大。

cues.en: When the residuals get too small, then the model is usually too complex and the model should also be relevant.
cues.zh: 殘差太小，模型通常就太複雜，而且模型也應該切合問題。

cues.en: So let's say, these are the characteristics of the real data, and now we have some ridiculous model.
cues.zh: 假設這是真實資料特徵，現在卻有個荒謬模型。

cues.en: This is our model of the world.
cues.zh: 這是世界模型。

cues.en: This is our template of how we think the world works.
cues.zh: 是我們認為世界如何運作的樣板。

cues.en: Now, when you try to map this template, this model onto the real data, it's not gonna explain anything in the real data.
cues.zh: 把這個樣板、模型套到真實資料，將無法解釋任何內容。

cues.en: So the residuals in this case will look just like the original data, more or less.
cues.zh: 所以這種情況的殘差，大致會和原始資料一樣。

cues.en: Residuals should be small, but models should be relevant and also simple.
